title: Meat Lover's Sheet Pan Pizza
seoTitle: Meat Lover's Sheet Pan Pizza | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Feeds the crew from one tray
subtitle: Feeds the crew from one tray
description: Feeds the crew from one tray. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Brown sausage and beef
steps.instruction: Cook Italian sausage and ground beef in a skillet over medium-high, breaking into fine crumbles until fully browned. Drain grease — greasy sheet pizza pools in the tray. Combine with cooked bacon and Canadian bacon in a bowl.

steps.title: Oil and stretch sheet pans
steps.instruction: Oil two half-sheet pans (18x13). Press and stretch dough to the corners; dock all over with a fork so air escapes. A tight fit feeds the crew from two trays instead of juggling four round pies.

steps.title: Par-bake crusts
steps.instruction: Par-bake at 425°F 8 minutes until set and pale golden — this carries the weight of five meats without a raw center.

steps.title: Sauce, cheese, and load meats
steps.instruction: Spread pizza sauce edge to edge. Layer mozzarella, then pepperoni, sausage-beef mix, and more mozzarella. Meat Lover's means crowded but not swimming — if toppings slide, you went too heavy in one spot.

steps.title: Bake until edges are crisp
steps.instruction: Bake at 425°F 18–22 minutes until cheese is deeply browned at the edges and the center reads 190°F on a thermometer through the cheese. Rotate pans halfway. Bottom should sound hollow when tapped on the pan edge.

steps.title: Rest and cut squares
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes so cheese sets — runny cheese burns rookies on the line. Cut into squares with a bench scraper; sprinkle parmesan. One tray feeds four; two trays feed eight with seconds.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Meat Lover's Sheet Pan Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Feeds the crew from one tray. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
